newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-South Australia to set up wool board.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-South Australia to set up wool board.

text.p: The South Australian government said on Wednesday it would set up a Wool Industry Development Board to advise on the sector's long-term strategic direction.

Primary Industries Minister Rob Kerin said in a statement he would call this month for expressions of interest from potential board members to develop a partnership approach between industry, the community and government.

Key issues to address could include strengthening customer linkages, developing key processing alliances, new markets and products, improving productivity techniques, increasing the production of quality wool, better marketing and achieving long-term industry sustainability, he said.

Kerin said the current plight of wool determined the wool board would be the first of a planned series of industry development boards, to be set up similar to boards of management in the private sector, for the state's primary industry sector.

"The (wool) industry is vital to South Australia as it represents about eight percent of the State's total export income and I recognise the need for the industry to develop a strategy for long-term stability," he said.
The board, expected to be in place by the end of 1996, would help determine the most effective way to maximise growth in the industry, including the most effective role for government, he said.
